title: The operation names of the six consumed rows and the SVAF order interface are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T5.1, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.1.2 integration points); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R9)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary; s13
description: The step consumes six rows across five owners and no source document publishes the operation name of any of them: the rwb-source-data data product that carries the appraisal of v_ace_valuation and the acceptance of valuation_ext, the SVAF order submission and the interface-run read of rwb-integration, the rule-in-force and decision-log read of rwb-decision, and the authorise operation of rwb-access. The SVAF interface has no identity, transport, order layout or failure code in any source either, and TSD S1 T5.1 declares no external system interface of this module at all. The baseline and the application story therefore build against a documented use and a placeholder, and no path, parameter or transport is invented.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations, no table, no event, no job and one workflow, and name no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists only API-S1-001 on /cases/{caseId}/route; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; FSD S1 A2.1.2 names the integration points as 'SVAF (order)' and the ACE collateral and valuation views and gives no operation; the FSD A2.1.2 step 1 names 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' as the trigger set and publishes no event name for it.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P2 rwb-integration owner, P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: Each owner publishes the operation name of its row before the wave 3 tag, and RWB-S1-E4001-CON replaces the placeholder with the published name in a minor version; the SVAF interface identity and transport are published by rwb-integration with its interface config.

title: The Ownership Map carries two valuation paths and no appraisal-order operation, and no source says which valuation path is current
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.1.2, A2.4.3.2)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.6 Schedules
description: Two documentation points meet in this baseline. The map gives S1 both POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations, which are the id-keyed and the business-keyed form of one operation, and no source says which is current after the D-RCV-35 re-base on ACE business keys. The map publishes no operation for the appraisal order itself, which leaves the step with the consumed interface run and the decision record as its only surface. The baseline declares only POST /cases/{caseId}/route, reads the business-key path as the current form and the id path as superseded, and declares no operation for the order.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations, POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations and POST /cases/{caseId}/route; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only; FSD S1 A2.1.2 names 'SVAF (order)' as the order path and no Workbench operation for it; FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 give valuation_key and asset_key as the business keys of an appraisal.
proposed: The service owner confirms at the tag which valuation path is current; the superseded one is retired in a major version of the sibling baseline and this baseline is unaffected.

title: The Ownership Map gives S1 no table while TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation as a new Workbench table and the FSD holds the acceptance in recovery.valuation_ext
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T3.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (document control change note, A2.4.3.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-001 Data table)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s18 Traceability; APP s3, s11, s12.7
description: Three sources read the appraisal store three ways. The ownership rows give S1 no table at all, so the service schema holds only the library objects of DP-03 and DP-09. TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation as a NEW Workbench table with DF-COL-018 to DF-COL-027, DF-COL-043 and DF-COL-044, including accepted, stale_flag and age_days. The FSD of v3 states that the acceptance and the stale flag are kept in recovery.valuation_ext, read on the ACE side, and the legacy Data table lists v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext rather than a Workbench table. On the higher-precedence reading the appraisal is ACE's and its acceptance is read on the rwb-source-data data product, so this baseline and the application story declare no table, and the store of the flag, the age and the acceptance is left open instead of being invented.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; TSD S1 T3.1 lists valuation as NEW with 14 Field IDs including DF-COL-027 accepted, DF-COL-043 stale_flag and DF-COL-044 age_days; the FSD S1 v3 change note and A2.4.3.2 place the acceptance in recovery.valuation_ext with valuation_key, asset_key and valuer_partner_id; the legacy Data table names v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext only.
area: Data model and ownership, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner confirms whether the Workbench-owned fields live in recovery.valuation_ext as a data product of rwb-source-data or in a valuation table of rwb_valuation; the DB story creates the table in its own Flyway sequence if it is S1's, and this baseline declares its elements in a minor version.

title: The application story consumes six rows and the SVAF order interface, and no source publishes their operation names
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.1.2); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T5.1, T5.3); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 to 7; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13
description: The step reads the appraisal and its acceptance from rwb-source-data, submits the order to rwb-integration, reads the interface run, reads the case state from rwb-case and the rule in force from rwb-decision, and authorises through rwb-access, and no source publishes an operation name, a parameter or a transport for any of those six rows. The plan gives this slice no class C dependency either, because the DP table of this legacy key adds none for DP-03, DP-05, DP-13 and DP-19, so the six rows are built against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the contract row carries the placeholder.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack name three S1 operations and no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only and T5.1 is the row 'None'; TSD S1 T5.3 is the row 'None'; the FSD S1 A2.1.2 integration points are 'SVAF (order)' and the ACE collateral and valuation views; the plan rows for RWB-S1-E4001-APP and -CON carry C as an empty list.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P2 rwb-integration owner, P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The five owners publish their operation names before the wave 3 tag; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use in the meantime, and a published name replaces the placeholder with no behaviour change.

title: No source fixes where the stale flag, the age and the acceptance are persisted for this step
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.4.3.2, A2.1.3.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-001 Data table)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 4 and 8; s8 BR2, BR5; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13
description: The legacy story reads and sets accepted, accepted_at, accepted_by, stale_flag and age_days in valuation_ext, TSD S1 T3.1 puts accepted, stale_flag and age_days on a NEW valuation table of the module, and the ownership rows give S1 no table, so no source says where those five values live after the split. The story computes the age and the stale flag per assessment, records them in the local decision record with the limit version, reads the acceptance on the rwb-source-data data product and writes no column of its own; the acceptance itself is the accept story's of this service.
evidence: The legacy Data table lists valuation_ext with DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049 including accepted, accepted_at, accepted_by, stale_flag and age_days; TSD S1 T3.1 gives DF-COL-027 accepted, DF-COL-043 stale_flag and DF-COL-044 age_days on the valuation table; the ownership rows of the context pack list no table for S1.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner names the column or the data-product field that holds the stale flag, the age and the acceptance; if it is a column of rwb_valuation the DB story adds it and the writer fills it, and until then the values live in the decision record only.

title: No S1 rule package is in force and no source names the age limit's parameter or the rule row of this step
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.1.3.1 BR-S1-001, A2.1.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-38 to R-UNI-40); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-001)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 4; s8 BR2, BR5; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and no S1 route rule id is in force for this feature: the routing logic carries no S1 rule row for the age check, and the S1 package is Phase 2 in the detailed design. No source names the parameter that holds the age limit either, nor the reference-data row that carries it, so the story reads whatever limit is in force with its version and records that version, and never writes a limit, an appraisal type or a threshold in code.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.1.3.1 gives BR-S1-001, that no value a business person may change is written in code and is read from reference data with its version, and A2.1.4.1 states the result is recorded with its rule version; the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries no S1 row for an appraisal age check; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE and no limit; the harness story of the same legacy key records that the S1 package is Phase 2.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule and reference-data owner names the limit parameter and publishes the S1 package, or confirms that the limit stays a reference-data row; the record then carries that rule id and version with no change to the step.

title: No source names the event or the timer that starts the age check on a completed ACE batch, and S1 owns no job and no event
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.1.2 step 1, A2.1.4.4); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 1; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules; CON s12.4, s12.6
description: FSD S1 A2.1.2 names three possible triggers of the step, 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', and A2.1.4.4 declares no background event for the feature. The ownership rows give S1 no job and no event, so no Schedule and no subscription exists to start the check when a batch completes, and the only trigger a source supports is the route command that starts RouteDecisionWorkflow. The story runs the check as the first step of that workflow and builds no timer and no subscription.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.1.2 step 1 gives the trigger set as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; FSD S1 A2.1.4.4 is the row 'None, No background event'; the ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no event and no job and one workflow, RouteDecisionWorkflow; TSD S1 T5.3 is the row 'None'.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: If the business needs the check to run on batch completion, the data owner publishes a readiness event or the service owner adds a Temporal Schedule covering the business date; until then the check runs inside the route decision only.
